title: Healing
lead: God is called Israel's healer (Exodus 15:26), and the Bible tells of sickness healed by prayer, by prophets and by Jesus and his apostles. Christians differ on whether healing is promised in Christ's atonement, and how far it should be expected now.

sections.b: At Marah God names himself "the LORD, your healer" (Exodus 15:26), and the Torah ties health and sickness to the covenant (Deuteronomy 7:15; Deuteronomy 28:27). The psalms pray for healing from illness that is often bound up with sin and enemies (Psalm 6:2; Psalm 38:3; Psalm 41:4) and praise God who "heals every sickness" (Psalm 103:3). Elijah and Elisha raise the dead and cleanse Naaman (1 Kings 17:17–24; 2 Kings 5). Isaiah's servant carries the people's sickness and pain (Isaiah 53:4–5), which Matthew applies to Jesus' healings (Matthew 8:16–17) and 1 Peter to forgiveness (1 Peter 2:24). The Gospels and Acts are full of healings, and James 5:14–16 tells the sick to call the elders to anoint them with oil and pray.
